patient: The tests found a tumour in the upper part of your right lung. It is a type of lung cancer called adenocarcinoma. Under the microscope the cells look very different from normal cells, which doctors call grade 3, and it means the tumour can grow faster. It had reached some lymph nodes in the middle of the chest, but scans found no spread to the brain or liver. You have finished chemotherapy and radiation, the tumour has shrunk, and you are now on an immunotherapy medicine to keep it under control. Your care team will explain what this means for you.
physician: Non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe, grade 3 (poorly differentiated, predominantly solid). Stage IIIA (cT2a N2 M0): a 3.2 cm primary with mediastinal lymphadenopathy; brain MRI and abdominal CT showed no metastases. EGFR and ALK negative, KRAS G12C mutated, PD-L1 tumour proportion score 60%. Treated with 4 cycles of cisplatin/pemetrexed with concurrent thoracic radiation to 60 Gy in 30 fractions, with partial response on restaging (1.8 cm). Now on durvalumab consolidation, and CEA has fallen from 12.5 to 5.2 ng/mL.
lab: Core biopsy shows invasive adenocarcinoma with a predominantly solid growth pattern and poor differentiation (grade 3). Immunohistochemistry is TTF-1 and Napsin A positive, supporting a lung primary, and Ki-67 is about 60%, a high proliferative fraction. PD-L1 by the 22C3 assay shows a tumour proportion score of 60%. Next-generation sequencing found a KRAS G12C mutation with a TP53 co-mutation, and no EGFR, ALK or ROS1 alterations. Serum CEA was 12.5 ng/mL at baseline and has fallen to 5.2 ng/mL, just above the 5.0 upper limit.
drug: Patient-specific: the tumour carries a KRAS G12C mutation and a TP53 co-mutation, has a PD-L1 tumour proportion score of 60%, and has no EGFR or ALK driver alteration. Background: G12C swaps glycine for cysteine at codon 12, keeping KRAS in its active GTP-bound state and driving MAPK signalling. Background: covalent KRAS G12C inhibitors such as sotorasib and adagrasib bind the mutant cysteine and lock KRAS in its inactive GDP-bound state. Background: durvalumab is an antibody against PD-L1 that stops it binding PD-1 on T cells, releasing a brake on the immune response against the tumour. Background: without EGFR or ALK alterations, those targeted drugs do not apply, and TP53 co-mutation is common in KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma.
